title.narrative: Public Expenditure Support Facility Program and Countercyclical Support Facility Support Program - PESF

description.narrative: The objective of the PESF is to accelerate reforms that are essential for long-term economic growth while also improving service delivery for social protection. The CSF will supplement the PESF by providing support to scale up the Government's countercyclical development program.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. More effective service delivery and expanded social safety net program (SSNP) Indicator: Application of the citizen report cards in at least 25% of the 40 poorest districts (FY2009 baseline: none) Progress/Status: Applied in 64 districts to target EGP for the poorest districts, an application broader than targeted

Output: 2. More conducive investment climate and larger Annual Development Program (ADP) implemented Indicator: At least 5 PPP projects identified and invited for private sector participation (FY2009 baseline: none) Progress/Status: The government created a fund titled ‘Bangladesh Infrastructure Finance Fund' (BIFF) to strengthen PPP activities and to encourage potential investors. Tk16 billion was placed in this fund from the allocation made for PPP in FY2010. One PPP project (Dhaka Elevated Express Way) has been identified so far and short-listing of firms through international bidding has been completed. Data Source: Government website

Output: 2. More conducive investment climate and larger Annual Development Program (ADP) implemented Indicator: Infrastructure Investment Fund and Viability Gap Fund in place (FY2009 baseline: no funds in place) Progress/Status: Both IIF and VGF are in place. Data Source: International Monetary Fund

Output: 2. More conducive investment climate and larger Annual Development Program (ADP) implemented Indicator: Resource allocation criteria for PPP infrastructure investment projects (FY2009 baseline: no criteria in place) Progress/Status: The allocation criteria have been defined in the revised policy and strategy for PPP which was adopted in August 2010. Data Source: Ministry of Planning

Output: 4. Private sector investment leveraged under public-private partnership (PPP) Indicator: At least five PPP projects identified and invited for private sector participation (FY2009 baseline: none)

Output: 3. Strengthened public financial management (PFM) Indicator: MTBF introduced in 20 ministries (FY2009 baseline: 16 ministries) Progress/Status: MTBF has been introduced and is operational in 33 ministries, more than the targeted number of ministries.

Output: 2. More conducive investment climate and larger Annual Development Program (ADP) implemented Indicator: Value of infrastructure projects under implementation rises by 20% over FY2009 levels (FY2009 estimated baseline: $2.8 billion implemented) Progress/Status: ADP actual spending increased by 34% to Tk259 billion ($3.7 million) in FY2010, more than the targeted increase. Data Source: Ministry of Finance

Output: 1. More effective service delivery and expanded social safety net program (SSNP) Indicator: 50% increase in the number of hardcore poor covered by the employment generation program (FY2009 baseline: 3.1 million) Progress/Status: In FY2010, 4.5 million hardcore poor were covered by the employment generation program, a number 46% higher than in FY2009. The increase was slightly below target. Data Source: Reports from civil society

Output: 1. More effective service delivery and expanded social safety net program (SSNP) Indicator: Gender-based budgeting completed in 20 ministries (FY2009 baseline: 4 ministries) Progress/Status: Completed in 33 ministries, more than the number targeted

Output: 1. More effective service delivery and expanded social safety net program (SSNP) Indicator: 25% increase in the number of vulnerable populations covered by the food security programs (FY2009 estimated baseline: 46.7 million) Progress/Status: The number of vulnerable populations covered by food security programs is estimated at 60.9 million, a 30% increase. Data Source: Government statistics

Output: 3. Strengthened public financial management (PFM) Indicator: Integrated budgeting and accounting system operational in all districts (FY2009 baseline: 55 districts) Progress/Status: IBAS oerational in all districts.

Output: 1. More effective service delivery and expanded social safety net program (SSNP) Indicator: 20% increase in the number of hardcore poor women supported by the Vulnerable Group Development Program (FY2009 baseline: 80,000 women) Progress/Status: 88,000 women were supported by the Vulnerable Group Development Program, the same number as in the revised FY2009 baseline Data Source: Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Social Welfare, and Ministry of Food and Disaster Management

Output: 2. More conducive investment climate and larger Annual Development Program (ADP) implemented Indicator: 10% increase in the level of foreign direct investments (FY2009 baseline: $882 million) Progress/Status: Preliminary estimates indicate that the level of foreign direct investment declined from a revised baseline of $808 million in FY2009 to $636 million in FY2010. Data Source: Bangladesh Bank

Output: 1. More effective service delivery and expanded social safety net program (SSNP) Indicator: 20% increase in the number of women covered by allowances for widowed, deserted, and destitute women (FY2009 baseline: 0.9 million women) Progress/Status: The target was not met. 0.9 million were covered by these allowances, the same number as in FY2009. Data Source: LGED reports

Output: 2. More conducive investment climate and larger Annual Development Program (ADP) implemented Indicator: The country's ranking in the World Bank Doing Business Survey reverts to the 2007 level (2009 baseline: 110th out of 181 countries) Progress/Status: The position of Bangladesh improved: it ranked 107th out of 183 countries in 2011 and 111th in 2010. Because of change in methology, comparison with 2007 is not available. Data Source: Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry

Output: 3. Strengthened public financial management (PFM) Indicator: Debt service liability management system introduced and implemented (FY2009 baseline: system being developed) Progress/Status: Debt service liability management systems are operational.
Output: 4. Private sector investment leveraged under public-private partnership (PPP) Indicator: Infrastructure Investment Fund and Viability Gap Fund in place (FY2009 baseline: no funds in place)

Output: 5. Assistance to affected export sector provided under FY2010 stimulus package Indicator: At least 50% of the budget allocation earmarked for export sector affected by global crisis, delivered

Stable macroeconomic environment where private sector development is emphasized, there is higher public and private investment, and where women and vulnerable populations have greater access to social services, including through effective gender targeting

Tax and non-tax revenue to GDP ratio will increase by 1 percentage point (FY2009 baseline: 11.2%) Progress/Status: The increase was better than the 1% targeted. The revenue to GDP ratio increased from 10.4% in FY2009 to 11.5% in FY2010, above past performances. The impact of the crisis on revenue in FY2009 was more severe than estimated under the baseline. Data Source: Ministry of Finance

Ratio of private investment to GDP will increase by 2 percentage points (FY2009 baseline: 19.6%) Progress/Status: From preliminary estimates, the ratio of private investment to GDP increased from 19.7% in FY2009 to 19.8% in FY2010, an increae less than 2 percentage points, yet sufficient to meet the targeted ratio. Data Source: Bangladesh Bank
Fiscal deficit remains within 5% of GDP (FY2009 estimated baseline: 4.1% of GDP)
Public investment rises to 4.8% of GDP in FY2010 (FY2009 baseline: 4.6% of GDP)

Food inflation will not exceed 10% (FY2009 estimated baseline: 6.7%) Progress/Status: Food inflation ceiling exceeded by small margin in 2010. Food inflation declined sharply in FY2009 from 6.8% in January 2009 (and 13.9% in July 2008) to 0.25% in June 2009, and remained below the 10% ceiling in 2009. But point-to point food inflation exceeded marginally the ceiling from January to June 2010. In FY2011 it fell again below 10% from July 2010. Data Source: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics

Coverage of women by women-targeted SSNPs increased by 20% (FY2009 estimated baseline: 7.2 million women) Progress/Status: The increase was less than targeted. The number of women covered by women-targeted SSNPs is estimated at 8.4 million in FY2010, a 17%% increase. Data Source: Reports from relevant government departments

Coverage of vulnerable people by social safety nets increases by 33% (FY2009 estimated baseline: 72 million people) Progress/Status: The coverage in FY 2010 was more than in FY2009, but less than targeted. The number of vulnerable people covered by SSNPs estimated at 89 million in FY2010, 23% more than in FY2009. Data Source: International Monetary Fund
